constituents.title: FINRA's New PFOF and Best Execution Guidance Education
constituents.one_line_claim: FINRA issued new guidance reiterating best execution obligations and prohibiting trade-offs between PFOF and price improvement
constituents.author: dlauer

constituents.title: FINRA fines Robinhood $70M
constituents.one_line_claim: FINRA issued a $70M enforcement action against Robinhood for PFOF violations and compliance failures including inadequate supervision and business continuity
constituents.author: dlauer

constituents.title: FINRA Posts Another Best Execution Notice
constituents.one_line_claim: FINRA reiterated best execution obligations and specified that firms cannot substitute PFOF payment for price improvement
constituents.author: dlauer

summary: This series by market structure commentator dlauer examines FINRA regulatory enforcement and guidance on payment for order flow (PFOF) issued in summer 2021. It reports on FINRA's new best-execution guidance targeting practices like Robinhood's, the June 2021 $70M fine against Robinhood for PFOF and compliance violations, and follow-up FINRA notices clarifying that brokers cannot trade off PFOF compensation against client price improvement. The work argues that accepting PFOF creates an inherent conflict with best-execution obligations and explains the mechanics of how market makers (Citadel, Virtu) structure rebates and PFOF payments.

key_claims.claim: Claims that FINRA issued guidance in 2021 reminding firms that best execution and best price obligations take priority over PFOF payments
key_claims.note: FINRA enforcement actions and guidance on PFOF and best execution are documented regulatory facts confirmed by hindsight record; EU subsequently banned PFOF by 2026

key_claims.claim: Claims that FINRA fined Robinhood $70M (with $57M in fines and $12.6M restitution) for PFOF violations and multiple compliance failures in 2021
key_claims.note: The June 2021 Robinhood FINRA enforcement action is documented in the hindsight record; Robinhood did pay fines for order-flow practices

key_claims.claim: Claims that a firm accepting PFOF mathematically cannot provide best execution and that this is the 'foundation of Robinhood's business model'
key_claims.note: The logical argument is sound and eventually validated by EU regulatory action banning PFOF, but the claim is stated as absolute rather than as regulatory principle; Robinhood continued operating but faced sustained pressure

key_claims.claim: Claims that FINRA guidance prohibits internalizers from offering brokers a choice between PFOF or price improvement
key_claims.note: This regulatory position on PFOF vs price improvement is documented in FINRA guidance referenced in the text

key_claims.claim: Claims that Robinhood collected $331M in PFOF in Q1 2021 and failed to exercise due diligence, supervise technology, and maintain proper business continuity
key_claims.note: Specific violations and PFOF revenue figures are from the FINRA enforcement action; confirmed in hindsight record

key_claims.claim: Claims that FINRA guidance could be an important regulatory step or provide fuel for class action lawsuits if not substantively enforced
key_claims.note: Vaguely hedged prediction; regulatory evolution on PFOF did occur but slowly; class actions did occur, though predicting their basis is speculative

validity_rationale: The work is grounded in primary sources (FINRA notices, enforcement actions) and accurately reports regulatory facts and mechanisms. The core claims about FINRA guidance and Robinhood enforcement are factually correct and validated by hindsight. The speculative elements (characterizing PFOF as 'mathematically impossible' alongside best execution, predicting regulatory or litigation outcomes) are modest, clearly labeled, and directionally validated by later regulatory moves (EU ban on PFOF by 2026). The market mechanics described are accurate. However, some vague predictions and the sample-only text coverage (pages 3-8 of 10) prevent a higher rating.
